content:
alex: Quick note from onboarding call: Python quickstart has multiple issues. The sample app in the repo fails on client init and a lot of example asset links 404. https://docs.redwood.ai/python/quickstart

alex: Error seen by customer: TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'api_key' when running the snippet in the repo.

luis: ugh, that's from the auth param rename (api_key -> token) that didn't propagate to the docs generator. can you paste the exact snippet?

alex: the docs currently show:
```python
from redwood import Client
import os
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
resp = client.generate("Test")
print(resp.text)
```
Traceback above on init.

emma: SDK now expects token=... and we also have AsyncClient for async apps. the correct sync example would be:
```python
from redwood import Client
import os
client = Client(token=os.getenv("REDWOOD_TOKEN"))
resp = client.generate("Test")
print(resp.text)
```
But better to show AsyncClient since many onboarding quickstarts use asyncio.

pete: also noticed the quickstart references `/v1/assets/getting-started.zip` which now lives under `/assets/v2/getting-started.zip` so the docs preview returns 404. Those assets power the sample app.

alex: filed a docs GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/1312 (quickstart auth + asset links). adding a small PR to update snippets + links.

luis: can we include a recommended async snippet and a streaming example that matches the SDK API? current async section shows `await client.stream(...)` but the sync section shows `.stream()` returning an iterator — inconsistent. propose this async streaming pattern for quickstart:
```python
from redwood import AsyncClient
import asyncio
import os

async def main():
    client = AsyncClient(token=os.getenv("REDWOOD_TOKEN"))
    # simple generate
    resp = await client.generate("Hello world", max_tokens=32)
    print(resp.text)

    # streaming (recommended when low-latency output is desired)
    async for chunk in client.stream("Write a 2-sentence haiku"):
        print(chunk.delta, end="")

asyncio.run(main())
```
That shows both generate + streaming.

emma: good. also we should add a typing note: `client: AsyncClient` and `from typing import AsyncIterator` in the snippet for clarity. many users rely on autocompletion and mypy flags.

pete: another DX: retry behavior isn't obvious in quickstart. customers assume 5xx are retried automatically. we only auto-retry idempotent requests. add a tiny block showing how to configure retries in the client: `retries=3`, `backoff_strategy='exponential'` or link to SDK config page.

alex: can infra add a redirect for old asset paths to avoid immediate breakage? a simple nginx redirect from `/v1/assets/*` to `/assets/v2/*` would buy us time.

infra-bot: pinging infra here: @infra-team please review redirect request. Suggested rule: 301 /v1/assets/(.*) -> /assets/v2/$1.

docs-ci: I added a quick CI e2e job draft that runs the quickstart snippet inside a virtualenv and checks the sample app runs end-to-end. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1315 (hotfix + e2e job opt-in).

luis: excellent. i'll add typing hints and a stub for `stream()` return type to improve editor hints. will also push a small change to the SDK to raise a clearer error when deprecated params are used (with a hint to the new `token` param).

emma: one more small UX ask: add a short blurb in the onboarding checklist for CSMs to avoid copy-pasting old saved replies pointing at the old quickstart. saved replies currently link to the outdated snippet.

alex: Support case 3567 opened. putting the customer on the PR preview for now.

pete: once PR merges, let's run the new CI job and keep the redirect in place for 2 weeks, then monitor 404 logs.

docs-ci: PR build queued. will post status here when green.

alex: thanks all — this is exactly the kind of snippet drift we want to catch early. drop other examples here if you find them and i'll batch-fix. :+1:
